thread:
support-jen: Pasting an escalation from a customer — intermittent SSE disconnects + partial payloads. They also saw a billing spike when clients kept reconnecting. Customer says it started after we enabled the new keepalive window. Logs attached.
eng-liz: Can you drop the minimal trace + sample client? Need the request id and any server-side write errors (EAGAIN/EPIPE).
support-jen: Quote from customer: "stream stopped mid-chunk, then client reconnect got 401 and double-billed for resumed session." They attached a capture showing repeated `writev` errors on the host.
ingest-omar: grabbing logs now. /var/log/redwood/streams/host-05.log shows repeated: `write: EAGAIN` then `socket abort: forced close (backpressure threshold)` around 2025-11-12T15:04:12Z.
ops-bot: [automated] incident id INC-20251112-431 attached: host-05 streaming write queue exceeded 2MB, aborted connection after 3 retries.
billing-sam: Noted the billing anomalies — multiple resume sessions incremented billing counters before dedupe. We're throttling for now until we confirm repro.
eng-liz: Two action items: (1) repro with a slow consumer locally, (2) collect kernel socket stats (sndbuf, sendq) and our server backpressure counters. I can try a repro with `nc` throttled.
support-jen: Customer willing to test with our guidance.
ingest-omar: Repro steps I used (worked locally):
```bash
# on host A (server) start a simple SSE toy
python3 -m http.server 8000 &
# on host B (client) simulate slow reader
tc qdisc add dev lo root tbf rate 20kbit burst 32k latency 50ms
nc localhost 8000
```
Result: server `write()` paused, kernel returned `EAGAIN` and then our runtime hit the abort threshold after 4s and closed the socket.
eng-liz: That aligns. Two problems: our abort threshold too aggressive for high-latency/throttled links; and billing resumed sessions earlier than dedupe window.
support-jen: Customer mentions auth 401 on reconnect — likely their token refresh flow races with reconnect ID. We should advise them to hold retry until token refresh completes.
eng-liz: Suggested short-term mitigations for the customer:
- increase client read buffer and implement exponential backoff for reconnects (avoid tight reconnect loops)
- use streaming keepalive header `X-Stream-Keepalive: 15s` to reduce TCP keepalive churn
- if using our SDK, upgrade to v1.4.2 (contains improved reconnect backoff)
ingest-omar: For server-side quick fix: bump backpressure abort from 4s -> 8s for the problematic pool, and lower the aggressive billing resume window from 1s to 250ms dedupe. I can push a canary change to staging.
ops-bot: [deploy] staging/backpressure-config updated by ingest-omar at 1739403100.
eng-liz: Also adding additional telemetry: increment counters when `EAGAIN` observed and emit `stream.backpressure.event` with sendq size and last-kv-length. Will add to console dashboard.
support-jen: Customer accepted canary. They will test tomorrow morning. Keep me posted.
billing-sam: I'll block any auto-invoice for affected org until we confirm dedupe fixes. :pray:
eng-liz: Tests to run for internal repro (short):
1) simulate slow consumer with `tc` throttle
2) run `strace -e write -p <pid>` to capture failing syscall
3) watch our `stream.write.retries` metric and `sendq_bytes`
Example strace snippet:
```bash
strace -e write -f -p <pid> -s 200
# look for: write(...)= -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
```
ingest-omar: I pushed a small test harness to staging: `/infra/stream-slow-consumer.sh`. It will spawn N producers and throttle a single consumer until we see abort.
support-jen: thanks. Once staging looks good, we'll schedule a single host deploy to the customer's region and coordinate testing window.
eng-liz: FYI: long-term we'll add graceful draining (queue snapshot + background flush) instead of hard abort, and tighten billing dedupe on reconnects.
support-jen: ack. I'll update the customer thread with these repro steps and the canary time.
eng-liz: ping me if they still see partial chunks; we may need to change our chunk flush semantics (flush on newline vs fixed-size flush) — that can avoid mid-chunk visible truncation.
support-jen: noted. :thumbsup:
billing-sam: following up on invoices after QA. :eyes:
ops-bot: [automated] follow-up ticket created: TICKET-20251112-789 assigned to eng-liz, ingest-omar, billing-sam.
support-jen: thread closing for now, will reopen if customer repros after canary.
